exercises.name: Walking
exercises.description: A natural, low-impact way to improve cardiovascular health and burn calories.
instructions: Maintain an upright posture with your head up and shoulders relaxed.
Swing your arms naturally and slightly with each step.
Step forward, landing on your heel and rolling through to your toe.
Maintain a steady, comfortable pace that allows you to breathe easily.
tips: Wear supportive footwear to protect your joints.
Keep your core slightly engaged to support your lower back.
Focus on a smooth, rhythmic stride.
exercises.notesForLlm: Low-impact cardio option useful for warmups, recovery, and deconditioned users.

exercises.name: Outdoor Running
exercises.description: A classic high-intensity cardio workout that builds endurance and burns significant calories.
instructions: Keep your head up and look about 10-20 feet ahead of you.
Maintain a relaxed upper body with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Land softly on the midfoot and push off with your toes.
Keep your core engaged and avoid leaning too far forward or backward.
tips: Start with a short warmup walk or light jog.
Increase your distance or intensity gradually to avoid injury.
Stay hydrated and wear appropriate running shoes.
exercises.notesForLlm: Higher-impact endurance option best when joints tolerate repeated ground contact.

exercises.name: Treadmill Walking
exercises.description: Walking on a treadmill allows for precise control of pace and incline in a controlled environment.
instructions: Step onto the treadmill and attach the safety clip to your clothing.
Start at a slow speed to get accustomed to the movement.
Maintain an upright posture and avoid holding onto the side rails for better balance and calorie burn.
Adjust speed and incline as needed to match your fitness level.
tips: Keep your eyes forward to maintain balance.
Use the incline feature to simulate outdoor walking and increase intensity.
Gradually decrease speed at the end of your session for a cooldown.

exercises.name: Treadmill Running
exercises.description: Running on a treadmill provides a consistent surface and the ability to track metrics easily.
instructions: Attach the safety clip and start with a slow walk to warm up.
Gradually increase the speed to your desired running pace.
Focus on landing softly on your midfoot and maintain a consistent rhythm.
Keep your core engaged and arms moving in a controlled manner.
tips: Vary your workouts with intervals of higher speed or incline.
Keep a water bottle nearby to stay hydrated.
Cool down with a few minutes of walking before stepping off.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
exercises.description: A low-impact cardio option that targets the lower body while being easy on the joints.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so there is a slight bend in your knee at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Sit upright or lean forward slightly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Pedal in a smooth, circular motion, pushing down and pulling up.
Adjust the resistance level to challenge your cardiovascular system.
tips: Ensure your feet are securely in the pedals or straps.
Maintain a consistent cadence (RPM) for better efficiency.
Don't lean too heavily on the handlebars.
exercises.notesForLlm: Low-impact cardio alternative when running is not ideal.

exercises.name: Elliptical
exercises.description: Provides a full-body, low-impact workout that mimics the motion of running without the impact.
instructions: Step onto the pedals and grasp the handles.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, either forward or backward.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight.
Use the handles to involve your upper body and increase total calorie burn.
tips: Focus on pushing through your entire foot, not just your toes.
Vary the resistance and incline to target different muscle groups.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid gripping the handles too tightly.
exercises.notesForLlm: Low-impact cardio option with simultaneous upper and lower body contribution.

exercises.name: Rowing
exercises.description: A powerful full-body workout that combines cardiovascular conditioning with strength building.
instructions: Sit on the seat and secure your feet in the straps.
The Catch: Lean forward slightly with arms extended and knees bent.
The Drive: Push through your legs, then lean back slightly and pull the handle toward your lower ribs.
The Finish: Legs are extended, handle is at your chest, and you are leaning back slightly.
The Recovery: Extend your arms, lean forward, and then bend your knees to return to the catch.
tips: Maintain a strong core and flat back throughout the motion.
The power should come 60% from legs, 20% from core, and 20% from arms.
Focus on a smooth, rhythmic motion and avoid jerking the handle.
exercises.notesForLlm: Full-body conditioning option that also trains pulling endurance.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
exercises.description: A high-intensity, portable cardio workout that improves coordination and agility.
instructions: Hold the handles with a relaxed grip, elbows close to your sides.
Jump only a few inches off the ground, just enough for the rope to pass under.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Use your wrists to rotate the rope, not your whole arms.
tips: Keep your core engaged and your shoulders relaxed.
Start with shorter intervals and gradually increase duration.
Maintain a consistent rhythm for better efficiency.
exercises.notesForLlm: High-impact conditioning drill with strong coordination demand.

exercises.name: Stair Climber
exercises.description: An effective way to build lower body strength and cardiovascular endurance by mimicking climbing stairs.
instructions: Step onto the machine and select your desired speed or program.
Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning heavily on the handrails.
Step with your whole foot and push through your heels to engage the glutes.
Keep your core engaged and your movements controlled.
tips: Vary your step height and speed to challenge different muscles.
Focus on a steady, sustainable pace.
Avoid skipping steps unless specifically programmed for advanced training.
exercises.notesForLlm: Cardio option with high local leg endurance demand.

exercises.name: SkiErg
exercises.description: A powerful full-body workout that simulates cross-country skiing, building endurance and upper-body strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles above your head.
Pull the handles down toward your hips while simultaneously hinging at the hips and bending your knees.
Finish the pull with your arms extended past your thighs.
Extend your hips and knees while returning the handles to the starting position.
tips: Use your core and legs to generate power, not just your arms.
Maintain a flat back and engaged core throughout the movement.
Focus on a smooth, continuous rhythm.
exercises.notesForLlm: High-intensity cardio option with significant upper-body and core engagement.

exercises.name: Air Squat
exercises.description: A foundational bodyweight movement that improves lower body strength and mobility.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to sit back into your hips.
Lower your body until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your weight on your heels, not your toes.
Ensure your knees stay in line with your toes and don't cave inward.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the entire movement.
exercises.notesForLlm: Foundational squat pattern useful for assessment, warmups, and high-rep work.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: Holding a weight at chest level while squatting helps improve form and core stability.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest with both hands.
Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your hips back and down, keeping your chest up and the weight close to your body.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed down and inside your knees at the bottom of the squat.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you push back up.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back.
exercises.notesForLlm: Accessible loaded squat pattern with a strong torso-bracing demand.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.description: The gold standard for building total-body strength and leg mass using a barbell.
instructions: Position the barbell across your upper back, resting on your traps.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Brace your core and lower your hips until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to an upright position.
tips: Keep your chest up and look slightly forward throughout the lift.
Avoid letting your knees cave inward.
Use a squat rack and a spotter for safety when lifting heavy.
exercises.notesForLlm: Primary bilateral lower-body strength lift with high technical and loading potential.

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.description: Placing the barbell on the front of the shoulders targets the quads and upper back more intensely.
instructions: Rest the barbell across the front of your shoulders, using either a 'clean' grip or a 'cross-arm' grip.
Keep your elbows high throughout the entire movement to stabilize the bar.
Squat down by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Drive back up to the starting position, keeping your torso upright.
tips: The bar should feel like it's resting on your deltoids, not your collarbone.
Maintain a tight core to support your upright posture.
Focus on keeping your heels on the ground.
exercises.notesForLlm: Quad-dominant squat variation with more upright posture and front-rack mobility demands.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.description: Squatting in a Smith machine provides extra stability, allowing you to focus on leg drive and positioning.
instructions: Position yourself under the bar with your feet slightly forward and shoulder-width apart.
Unlatch the bar and lower your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position.
Latch the bar securely after completing your reps.
tips: Keep your chest up and core engaged throughout the movement.
Experiment with foot placement to target different parts of your legs.
The Smith machine's fixed path reduces balance demands.
exercises.notesForLlm: Guided squat variation with lower stability demand.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Squat
exercises.description: Holding dumbbells at your sides while squatting is an accessible way to add resistance to the basic squat movement.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Lower your hips back and down as if sitting in a chair, keeping your chest up.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to return to an upright position.
tips: Keep the weights steady at your sides; don't let them swing.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Great for those who find barbell squats uncomfortable.
exercises.notesForLlm: Accessible loaded squat variation with dumbbells held at the sides.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: A machine-based press that allows for heavy lower body loading with minimal back strain.
instructions: Sit in the machine with your back and head flat against the padded support.
Place your feet on the platform about shoulder-width apart.
Release the safety bars and lower the platform toward your chest by bending your knees.
Push the platform back to the starting position without locking your knees at the top.
tips: Avoid lifting your lower back off the seat.
Keep your feet flat on the platform at all times.
Control the weight during both the lowering and pushing phases.
exercises.notesForLlm: Machine-based lower-body press that reduces balance demands.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.description: A functional movement that builds single-leg strength, balance, and coordination.
instructions: Step forward with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Ensure your front knee is directly above your ankle.
Drive through the front heel to stand up and step forward with the other leg.
Continue alternating legs as you walk forward.
tips: Keep your torso upright and your core engaged.
Don't let your back knee touch the floor with impact.
Maintain your balance by focusing on a spot in front of you.
exercises.notesForLlm: Dynamic unilateral leg pattern with high balance and coordination demand.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: Step backward into a lunge to target the glutes and hamstrings with less knee pressure.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Step backward with one foot and lower your hips until both knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle.
Push off with your back foot to return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your weight primarily on the front foot.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
Control the descent to avoid banging your back knee on the floor.
exercises.notesForLlm: Often more knee-friendly than forward-stepping lunge variations.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.description: Elevate your rear foot to place intense focus and stretch on the front leg's quads and glutes.
instructions: Stand a few feet in front of a bench and place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Lower your hips until your front thigh is almost parallel to the floor.
Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your foot and doesn't pass your toes.
Drive through the front heel to return to an upright position.
tips: Focus on keeping your torso upright or with a slight forward lean.
This exercise requires significant balance; start with bodyweight before adding dumbbells.
Adjust your distance from the bench to find the most comfortable and effective position.
exercises.notesForLlm: High-tension unilateral lower-body lift; can also be loaded with dumbbells if available.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.description: Step onto an elevated surface to build powerful glutes and improve functional leg strength.
instructions: Place one foot on a sturdy bench or box.
Drive through that heel to lift your body onto the platform.
Step down with the other foot first, followed by the starting foot.
Alternate legs or complete all reps on one side before switching.
tips: Keep your core engaged and your chest up.
Try not to push off the floor with your trailing foot; let the elevated leg do the work.
Control your descent to protect your joints.
exercises.notesForLlm: Useful unilateral pattern that can be scaled easily with step height.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that specifically targets and builds the quadriceps muscles.
instructions: Sit in the leg extension machine with your back against the pad.
Place your shins behind the padded lever.
Extend your legs until they are straight, focusing on the contraction in your quads.
Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift the weight.
Don't lock your knees forcefully at the top.
Ensure the padded lever is positioned just above your ankles.
exercises.notesForLlm: Single-joint quad accessory best used for hypertrophy, not as a primary movement.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curl
exercises.description: Focuses on isolating the hamstrings for improved strength and knee stability.
instructions: Lie face down on the leg curl machine with your legs fully extended.
Position the padded lever just above your heels.
Curl your legs up as far as possible, squeezing your hamstrings at the top.
Lower the weight back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
tips: Keep your hips pressed against the bench throughout the movement.
Focus on a slow and controlled eccentric (lowering) phase.
Avoid swinging the weight.
exercises.notesForLlm: Single-joint hamstring accessory that pairs well with squat-dominant days.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.description: Isolates the hamstrings in a seated position for maximum contraction and muscle building.
instructions: Sit in the machine and adjust the lap pad so it rests firmly against your thighs.
Place your legs over the padded lever so it sits behind your ankles.
Curl your legs down and back as far as possible.
Slowly return the lever to the starting position.
tips: Maintain a stable upper body and avoid using your arms to help pull.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the bottom of the movement.
Keep your feet flexed throughout the set.
exercises.notesForLlm: Stable machine isolation for the hamstrings; good for hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.description: Strengthens and builds the calf muscles by lifting your heels off the ground.
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step or platform with the balls of your feet.
Lower your heels below the level of the step to stretch your calves.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Lower back down slowly to the starting stretch position.
tips: Hold onto a wall or rail for balance if needed.
Pause for a second at the top to maximize contraction.
Can be performed on one leg at a time to increase difficulty.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Widely considered the best exercise for maximum glute development and strength.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a barbell across your hips.
Plant your feet firmly on the ground, about shoulder-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips back toward the floor.
tips: Use a pad or towel on the barbell for comfort.
Keep your chin tucked and your core engaged to protect your lower back.
Don't overextend your lower back at the top of the movement.
exercises.notesForLlm: Glute-focused bilateral hinge variation with lower spinal loading than deadlifts.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A bodyweight floor exercise that activates the glutes and improves hip extension.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Keep your arms at your sides with palms down.
Lift your hips off the floor by squeezing your glutes and pushing through your heels.
Hold the position for a second at the top, then lower back down.
tips: Ensure your core is engaged so your lower back doesn't arch excessively.
Focus on using your glutes rather than your lower back or hamstrings.
For an added challenge, perform the bridge with one leg extended.
exercises.notesForLlm: Beginner-friendly hip extension pattern useful in warmups and early strength work.

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.description: A fundamental lift for total body strength, targeting the entire posterior chain.
instructions: Stand with your mid-foot under the barbell.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the bar just outside your legs.
Keep your back flat and chest up as you drive through your heels to stand up.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the movement and stand fully upright.
tips: Don't round your back; maintain a neutral spine.
Inhale and brace your core before you pull the weight.
Lower the bar by hinging at the hips first, then bending your knees once the bar clears them.
exercises.notesForLlm: Primary bilateral hinge with high systemic fatigue and loading potential.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A deadlift variation that emphasizes the stretch and contraction of the hamstrings.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs.
Hinge at the hips and lower the bar toward the floor while keeping your legs mostly straight (slight bend in knees).
Lower the bar until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to return to the starting position.
tips: Keep the bar very close to your legs at all times.
Focus on pushing your hips back as far as possible.
Avoid rounding your shoulders or lower back.
exercises.notesForLlm: Posterior-chain hinge emphasizing hamstrings and controlled eccentric loading.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hamstring-focused hinge using dumbbells, which allows for a more natural range of motion.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Hinge at your hips and lower the weights toward your feet, keeping your back flat.
Lower until you feel a good stretch in your hamstrings.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to return to a standing position.
tips: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs throughout the movement.
Focus on pushing your hips back rather than reaching for the floor.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees.
exercises.notesForLlm: Dumbbell hinge variation emphasizing hamstrings with more freedom of movement than a barbell.

exercises.name: Machine Glute Kickback
exercises.description: A targeted machine exercise that isolates the glutes through a kickback motion.
instructions: Position yourself in the machine and place one foot on the platform.
Push the platform back and up by extending your hip.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
tips: Maintain a stable core and avoid arching your back.
Keep the movement controlled and focus on the glute contraction.
Don't swing your leg; use your muscles to move the weight.
exercises.notesForLlm: Unilateral glute isolation; great for shaping and strengthening the posterior chain.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
exercises.description: Uses cable resistance to isolate the glutes through a controlled kickback motion, providing constant tension throughout the range of motion.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to the cable machine at the lowest setting and fasten it around one ankle.
Stand facing the machine and hold the frame for balance.
Keeping your core tight and a slight bend in the standing leg, kick the strapped leg back and up by extending your hip.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating your hips.
Move through the full range of hip extension to maximize glute activation.
Control the weight on the way back down rather than letting the cable pull your leg forward.
exercises.notesForLlm: Unilateral cable glute isolation; the cable provides constant tension unlike the machine version, making it effective for both strength and hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Machine Hip Abduction
exercises.description: Targets the outer hips and glute medius to improve hip stability and aesthetics.
instructions: Sit in the machine with your outer thighs against the pads.
Push your legs outward against the resistance.
Pause for a second at the point of maximum contraction.
Slowly bring your legs back together.
tips: Keep your back flat against the seat.
Use a controlled tempo for both the opening and closing phases.
Adjust the starting position to a comfortable range of motion.
exercises.notesForLlm: Isolation for hip abductors; important for lateral stability.

exercises.name: Machine Hip Adduction
exercises.description: Strengthens the inner thigh muscles (adductors) for improved leg stability.
instructions: Sit in the machine with your inner thighs against the pads.
Squeeze your legs together against the resistance.
Pause for a second at the point of maximum contraction.
Slowly allow your legs to return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your upper body stable throughout the set.
Focus on using your inner thigh muscles, not your feet.
Don't let the weights slam together at the end of the rep.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.description: Uses a cable and ankle strap to isolate the outer hips and glute medius one side at a time.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable pulley and secure it around the outside leg.
Stand side-on to the machine and hold the frame for balance.
Move the working leg out to the side against the cable while keeping your torso mostly still.
Pause briefly, then return with control to the starting position.
tips: Keep the movement small and controlled rather than swinging the leg.
Brace your core so the hip does the work instead of your trunk.
Slightly turn the toes forward to better target the glute medius.
exercises.notesForLlm: Unilateral cable abductor isolation using an ankle strap; useful for hip stability and glute medius development.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Adduction
exercises.description: Uses a cable and ankle strap to strengthen the inner thigh muscles one side at a time.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable pulley and secure it around the inside leg.
Stand side-on to the machine with the working leg farthest from the stack and hold the frame for balance.
Sweep the working leg across the front of your body against the resistance.
Pause briefly, then return to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating your hips.
Move slowly so the inner thigh controls both directions of the rep.
Use a light to moderate load and focus on the squeeze at the end range.
exercises.notesForLlm: Unilateral cable adductor isolation using an ankle strap; useful for groin strength and hip balance.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.description: An explosive movement that builds lower-body power and improves cardiovascular fitness.
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and swing your arms back, then explosively jump onto the box.
Land softly in a partial squat with both feet entirely on the box.
Stand up fully, then step back down one foot at a time.
tips: Focus on a quiet landing to ensure you are absorbing the impact.
Choose a box height that allows for proper landing form.
Don't jump back down; stepping down is safer for your joints.
exercises.notesForLlm: High-impact plyometric drill for power development.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: A classic bodyweight exercise that builds chest, shoulder, and triceps strength.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle.
Push through your palms to return to the starting position.
tips: Don't let your lower back sag; keep your core tight.
Focus on a full range of motion for better muscle engagement.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you push back up.
exercises.notesForLlm: Scalable horizontal press that works well from complete beginner to advanced via modifications.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.description: Perform push-ups with your feet elevated on a bench to place more emphasis on the upper chest and shoulders.
instructions: Place your feet on a flat bench and your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels, engaging your core.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Push back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
tips: Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Don't let your hips sag; keep your glutes and core tight.
The higher the bench, the more difficult the exercise becomes.
exercises.notesForLlm: Upper-chest focused push-up variation requiring more shoulder stability.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.description: The fundamental upper body lift for developing maximum chest and arm power.
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower the bar to your mid-chest in a controlled manner.
Drive the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades retracted (squeezed together) throughout the lift.
Maintain a slight arch in your lower back, but keep your glutes on the bench.
Use a spotter, especially when lifting heavy weights.
exercises.notesForLlm: Primary bilateral horizontal press with strong strength carryover.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Pressing dumbbells while lying on a flat bench allows for a greater range of motion and improved shoulder health.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level.
Press the weights upward until your arms are fully extended over your chest.
Lower the dumbbells with control until they are level with your chest.
Maintain a stable core and feet flat on the floor.
tips: Focus on bringing the dumbbells together at the top without touching them.
Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Dumbbells require more stabilization than a barbell.
exercises.notesForLlm: Dumbbell horizontal press providing more shoulder freedom and ROM.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.description: The Smith machine provides a guided path for the bench press, making it safer for those training alone and allowing for intense muscle focus.
instructions: Lie on the bench and position it so the bar aligns with your mid-chest.
Unlatch the bar and lower it slowly to your chest.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Latch the bar securely when finished.
tips: Ensure the bench is perfectly centered under the bar.
Focus on the contraction in your chest throughout the movement.
A great option for isolation and drop sets.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press
exercises.description: An upward-angled press that targets the upper portion of the chest and shoulders.
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30-45 degree incline.
Sit with your back against the bench and feet flat on the floor.
Press the dumbbells upward from shoulder height until your arms are extended over your chest.
Lower the weights back to shoulder level with control.
tips: Don't let the dumbbells drift too far forward or backward.
Focus on squeezing your upper chest at the top of the movement.
Maintain a stable core to avoid excessive arching.
exercises.notesForLlm: Upper-chest biased press; dumbbell implementation offers more shoulder freedom.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
exercises.description: Pressing dumbbells on an incline bench emphasizes the upper chest while allowing each arm to move independently.
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30-45 degree incline.
Sit with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, then lean back against the bench.
Press the dumbbells upward from upper-chest level until your arms are extended.
Lower the weights back to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades retracted against the bench.
Use a moderate incline to keep the emphasis on your upper chest.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout the press.
exercises.notesForLlm: Upper-chest biased press performed with independent dumbbells.

exercises.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press
exercises.description: Pressing a barbell on an incline bench targets the upper chest and shoulders while allowing for heavier loads.
instructions: Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline and position yourself under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower the bar to your upper chest in a controlled manner.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked slightly, not flared completely to the sides.
Ensure the bar touches your upper chest, not your neck.
Use a spotter for safety.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
exercises.description: A guided incline press that isolates the upper chest and allows for safe training near failure.
instructions: Set the adjustable bench to an incline and center it under the Smith machine bar.
Lie on the bench and ensure the bar aligns with your upper chest.
Unlatch the bar and lower it with control toward your chest.
Press the bar back to the starting position.
tips: Focus on a smooth, consistent tempo.
Adjust the bench position to find the most comfortable pressing line.
Excellent for finishing off the upper chest.

exercises.name: Barbell Decline Bench Press
exercises.description: Pressing on a decline targets the lower portion of the chest and often allows for heavier loading due to the mechanical advantage.
instructions: Secure your feet in the decline bench and lie back.
Grip the barbell with a medium-width grip.
Lower the bar to your lower chest/upper abs area.
Press the bar back up to the starting position.
tips: Have a spotter help you unrack and rack the bar.
Keep the movement controlled; don't bounce the bar off your chest.
Focus on the contraction in the lower chest.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Decline Bench Press
exercises.description: Dumbbell decline press provides a deep stretch for the lower chest and improved range of motion.
instructions: Sit on the end of a decline bench with dumbbells on your thighs.
Lie back while bringing the weights to your chest level.
Press the dumbbells upward until arms are extended.
Lower them back down with control.
tips: Be careful when getting into and out of position with heavy dumbbells.
Focus on the squeeze at the top of the movement.
Keep your core engaged.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Decline Bench Press
exercises.description: A guided decline press that safely targets the lower chest muscles.
instructions: Position a decline bench under the Smith machine bar.
Lie down and ensure the bar path is over your lower chest.
Unlatch the bar and lower it toward your chest with control.
Press the bar back to the starting position.
tips: Ensure the bench is securely positioned and centered.
Keep your back flat against the bench.
Great for high-volume chest work.

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.description: Provides a stable and controlled way to target the chest muscles with reduced balance requirements.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so the handles are aligned with your mid-chest.
Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position.
tips: Keep your elbows slightly below your shoulder level.
Maintain contact between your back and the pad at all times.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top.
exercises.notesForLlm: Stable machine press that lowers coordination demands.

exercises.name: Chest Fly
exercises.description: An isolation movement that stretches and defines the chest muscles.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with dumbbells held over your chest, palms facing each other.
Lower the weights out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your chest, then bring the weights back together over your chest.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the top.
tips: Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Avoid going too deep if you feel any shoulder discomfort.
Focus on the 'hugging a tree' motion.
exercises.notesForLlm: Accessory chest isolation movement; use lighter loads and higher control.

exercises.name: Cable Fly
exercises.description: Uses cables to provide constant tension on the chest muscles through the entire range of motion.
instructions: Stand between two cable pulleys with handles at chest height.
Step forward slightly and hold the handles with your arms extended to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Focus on the contraction in your chest as you bring your hands together.
Maintain a slight forward lean for better stability.
Keep your core tight to prevent your body from swaying.
exercises.notesForLlm: Cable-based chest isolation with smoother resistance than dumbbell flyes.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch Press
exercises.description: A kneeling cable ab exercise that overloads the crunch pattern to build stronger, more defined abdominal muscles.
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel facing the cable machine.
Hold the rope beside your head and brace your hips so the movement comes from your torso.
Crunch your ribcage down toward your pelvis while keeping your elbows close and abs fully engaged.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack yank you upright.
tips: Think about curling your spine one segment at a time instead of just pulling with your arms.
Keep your hips mostly fixed so your abs, not your hip flexors, do the work.
Use a controlled load that lets you fully shorten the abs on every rep.
exercises.notesForLlm: Loaded cable crunch for anterior-core hypertrophy; treat it as a reps-based ab accessory rather than a chest press.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
exercises.description: Setting the cables high and pulling downward targets the lower fibers of the chest.
instructions: Set the cable pulleys to the highest position.
Grip the handles and step forward with one foot for stability.
Pull the handles down and together in front of your waist.
Slowly return your arms to the starting high position.
tips: Squeeze your lower chest at the bottom of the movement.
Maintain a slight forward lean.
Avoid using your body weight to pull the cables.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
exercises.description: Setting the cables low and pulling upward targets the upper chest and front deltoids.
instructions: Set the cable pulleys to the lowest position.
Grip the handles and stand in the center, stepping slightly forward.
Pull the handles upward and together in front of your upper chest.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting low position.
tips: Focus on the contraction in your upper chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Control the weight during the entire movement.

exercises.name: Pec Deck Fly
exercises.description: A machine-based fly that provides consistent tension on the chest for better isolation.
instructions: Sit in the machine and place your forearms against the padded levers.
Grip the handles and pull the levers together in front of your chest.
Pause for a second at the point of maximum contraction.
Slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your back and head against the seat.
Focus on squeezing with your chest rather than pulling with your arms.
Maintain a consistent, controlled tempo.
exercises.notesForLlm: Very stable chest isolation; allows for high intensity with low stability demand.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.description: A powerful vertical press that builds broad shoulders and upper body stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip.
Brace your core and press the bar directly overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lock out your elbows at the top and push your head slightly forward.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders with control.
tips: Don't use your legs to help lift the weight (that's a push press).
Keep your core and glutes tight to stabilize your torso.
Focus on a vertical bar path.
exercises.notesForLlm: Primary vertical press that requires good shoulder mobility and trunk control.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: Pressing dumbbells overhead allows for a natural range of motion and helps address muscle imbalances.
instructions: Stand or sit with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing forward.
Press the weights upward until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control.
Keep your core engaged to avoid arching your back.
tips: Focus on a smooth, controlled press.
Maintain a stable base whether sitting or standing.
Dumbbells offer more freedom for the shoulder joint than a barbell.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Overhead Press
exercises.description: A guided vertical press that allows you to focus purely on shoulder drive with added safety.
instructions: Position a seat or stand under the Smith machine bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unlatch the bar and press it overhead until arms are extended.
Lower it back to shoulder level and repeat.
tips: Ensure your positioning allows for a safe vertical bar path.
Focus on squeezing your deltoids at the top.
Avoid excessive arching of the lower back.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.description: A shoulder press with a rotational component that hits all three heads of the deltoids.
instructions: Sit or stand with dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you.
Press the weights overhead while rotating your palms forward.
Finish with your arms extended overhead and palms facing away.
Rotate your palms back toward you as you lower the weights to the starting position.
tips: Maintain a controlled rotation throughout the press.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Avoid using excessively heavy weights until you master the coordination.
exercises.notesForLlm: Dumbbell shoulder press variation with larger shoulder ROM.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.description: The key isolation exercise for building width in the shoulders.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows until they are level with your shoulders.
Pause for a second at the top, then slowly lower the weights back to your sides.
tips: Don't swing the weights or use momentum.
Lead with your elbows, not your wrists.
Imagine you are pouring water out of a pitcher at the top of the movement.
exercises.notesForLlm: Shoulder accessory movement typically programmed with moderate to high reps.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: A lateral raise using a cable machine to provide constant tension on the side deltoids throughout the entire movement.
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with the pulley at the lowest setting.
Grip the handle with the far hand and pull it across your body, or with the near hand behind your back.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is level with your shoulder, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
tips: Maintain a tall posture and avoid leaning away from the machine.
Focus on leading with your elbow and keep the movement controlled.
The cable provides tension even at the bottom of the rep, unlike dumbbells.
exercises.notesForLlm: Side-deltoid isolation with constant tension; excellent for hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Front Raise
exercises.description: Targets the front part of the shoulders for better definition and strength.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Lift the weights forward and up until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause for a second, then lower the weights back down with control.
tips: Keep your core tight to avoid rocking your body.
Don't lift the weights above shoulder level.
Can be performed alternating arms or both together.
exercises.notesForLlm: Anterior-shoulder accessory with relatively low loading needs.

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise
exercises.description: Isolates the front deltoids using cable resistance for smooth, constant tension.
instructions: Stand facing away from a cable machine with the pulley at the lowest setting.
Hold the handle (or a bar attachment) between your legs or at your side.
Lift your arm(s) forward and up until they are level with your shoulders.
Slowly lower back to the starting position.
tips: Keep your core engaged to prevent your torso from swaying.
Control the weight throughout the entire range of motion.
Avoid using momentum to lift the weight.
exercises.notesForLlm: Front-deltoid isolation with cable resistance.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: Isolates the rear deltoids using cables, allowing for a consistent resistance profile.
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable crossover machine with the pulleys at head height.
Cross your arms and grab the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand.
Pull the handles out and back in a wide arc, squeezing your rear delts.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining tension.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Focus on pulling with your shoulders, not your back muscles.
Stand tall and keep your core tight.
exercises.notesForLlm: Posterior-deltoid isolation with constant cable tension.

exercises.name: Cable Upright Row
exercises.description: Targets the shoulders and traps by pulling a cable attachment vertically toward the chin.
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with the pulley at the lowest setting and a straight bar attached.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar vertically toward your chin, leading with your elbows.
Stop when the bar is at chest height and your elbows are high.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
tips: Keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders too much; focus on the deltoids.
Maintain a stable, upright posture.
exercises.notesForLlm: Shoulder and trap movement; lead with elbows and control the descent.

exercises.name: Cable External Rotation
exercises.description: Strengthens the rotator cuff by rotating the arm outward against cable resistance.
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with the pulley at elbow height.
Grip the handle with the far hand, keeping your elbow tucked into your side at a 90-degree angle.
Rotate your forearm outward away from your body as far as comfortable.
Slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Place a towel between your elbow and your side to ensure your arm stays tucked.
Use a very light weight; this is about joint health and stability, not maximum load.
Move with control and through a comfortable range of motion.
exercises.notesForLlm: Rotator-cuff stability exercise; crucial for shoulder health and injury prevention.

exercises.name: Cable Internal Rotation
exercises.description: Strengthens the internal rotators of the shoulder using a cable machine.
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with the pulley at elbow height.
Grip the handle with the near hand, keeping your elbow tucked into your side at a 90-degree angle.
Rotate your forearm inward toward your body.
Slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your elbow pinned to your side throughout the set.
Focus on the quality of the movement rather than the weight.
Maintain a tall, stable posture.
exercises.notesForLlm: Rotator-cuff stability exercise targeting the internal rotators.

exercises.name: Triceps Dip
exercises.description: A demanding bodyweight exercise that builds serious power in the triceps and chest.
instructions: Grip the parallel bars and push yourself up until your arms are fully extended.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Keep your torso mostly upright to focus on the triceps.
tips: Avoid letting your shoulders shrug toward your ears.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your body.
If bodyweight is too difficult, use an assisted dip machine or bands.
exercises.notesForLlm: Demanding bodyweight press with large shoulder extension range.

exercises.name: Chest Dip
exercises.description: A dip variation where you lean your torso forward to shift the focus from the triceps to the chest muscles.
instructions: Grip the parallel bars and push yourself up to the starting position.
Lean your torso forward at about a 45-degree angle as you lower your body.
Allow your elbows to flare out slightly as you descend.
Push back up to the starting position while maintaining the forward lean.
tips: Squeeze your chest at the top of the movement.
Lower yourself until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Control the descent to avoid shoulder strain.
exercises.notesForLlm: Chest-focused dip variation; emphasize the forward lean throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: A popular cable exercise for isolating and building the back of the arms.
instructions: Attach a bar or rope to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Grip the attachment and pull it down until your elbows are at a 90-degree angle.
Push the attachment down until your arms are fully extended, squeezing your triceps at the bottom.
Slowly return to the 90-degree starting position.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout the set.
Avoid using your body weight to push the cable down.
Maintain a slight forward lean and engaged core.
exercises.notesForLlm: Simple triceps accessory that is easy to place after compound pressing.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Targets the long head of the triceps by extending the weight overhead.
instructions: Sit or stand, holding a dumbbell with both hands overhead.
Lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms to lift the weight back to the starting position overhead.
Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed forward rather than out to the sides.
Don't let your lower back arch excessively; keep your core tight.
Use a controlled tempo to avoid hitting your head or neck.
exercises.notesForLlm: Long-head triceps accessory with overhead mobility demand.

exercises.name: Cable Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.description: A cable version of the overhead triceps extension that keeps constant tension on the long head of the triceps through the full range of motion.
instructions: Attach a rope to a low cable or position yourself so the cable tracks behind your head.
Face away from the machine and bring the rope overhead with elbows bent and pointed forward.
Extend your elbows until your arms are straight, squeezing the triceps at the top.
Slowly return to the stretched starting position without letting your elbows flare excessively.
tips: Keep your elbows mostly fixed in place and let only the forearms move.
Brace your core so your lower back does not arch during the set.
Use a smooth tempo and take advantage of the stretch at the bottom.
exercises.notesForLlm: Cable-based long-head triceps accessory; often easier to load smoothly than the dumbbell version.

exercises.name: Ring Dip
exercises.description: An advanced dip variation on rings that requires significant stability and strength.
instructions: Support yourself on the rings with arms fully extended.
Lower your body with control, keeping the rings close to your sides.
Drive back up to the starting position, focusing on stabilizing the rings.
Turn your palms out slightly at the top for maximum stability.
tips: Keep your core extremely tight to minimize swinging.
Start with ring holds to build the necessary stability before attempting full reps.
Ensure the rings are at an appropriate height for your range of motion.
exercises.notesForLlm: High-stability demand dip; much harder than stationary dips.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.description: An elite bodyweight movement for building a wide, powerful back and strong arms.
instructions: Grip the bar with your palms facing away from you, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Hang with your arms fully extended and your core engaged.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down toward your hips.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than just your arms.
Avoid swinging your legs or using momentum (kipping).
If you can't perform a full pull-up, start with assisted variations or negatives.
exercises.notesForLlm: Advanced bodyweight vertical pull; scale volume carefully.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.description: A pull-up variation with palms facing you, emphasizing the biceps and lower lats.
instructions: Grip the bar with your palms facing toward you, about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended.
Pull your chin over the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
tips: Chin-ups generally recruit more biceps and chest than pull-ups.
Keep your core tight to prevent your body from swinging.
Ensure a full range of motion from a dead hang to chin over the bar.
exercises.notesForLlm: Supinated vertical pull, often slightly easier than pull-ups.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A machine-based exercise that allows you to build vertical pulling strength in a controlled way.
instructions: Sit in the machine and adjust the knee pads so you are securely held in place.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width and lean back slightly.
Pull the bar down toward your upper chest, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position.
tips: Don't pull the bar behind your neck; pull it to your upper chest.
Focus on leading with your elbows.
Control the weight on the way up to maintain tension in your lats.
exercises.notesForLlm: Accessible vertical pulling alternative to pull-ups.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: Targets the thickness of the back by pulling cables toward the torso while seated.
instructions: Sit with your feet on the platforms and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the handle and sit up straight with your arms extended.
Pull the handle toward your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack slam.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rocking your torso back and forth.
Focus on pulling with your elbows rather than your hands.
Maintain a stable core throughout the movement.
exercises.notesForLlm: Stable horizontal pulling option with broad loading range.

exercises.name: Seated Machine Row
exercises.description: A chest-supported machine row that isolates the back muscles while protecting the lower back.
instructions: Adjust the seat and chest pad so you can comfortably reach the handles with arms extended.
Sit with your chest against the pad and grip the handles.
Pull the handles toward you, focusing on the contraction in your mid-back.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position.
tips: Keep your chest pressed firmly against the pad to isolate your back.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades at the point of maximum contraction.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders.
exercises.notesForLlm: Stable, chest-supported row; excellent for back hypertrophy without lower back fatigue.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: A powerful compound movement that builds back thickness and overall upper body strength.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees slightly, keeping your back flat.
Pull the barbell toward your lower ribs, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Lower the bar back to the starting position with control.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back.
Keep your core engaged to support your lower back.
Don't use momentum to 'cheat' the weight up.
exercises.notesForLlm: Heavy horizontal pull with significant trunk endurance demand.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: Bending over and pulling dumbbells toward your waist targets the back muscles with a more flexible range of motion.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Pull the dumbbells toward your hips, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the weights back down with control.
tips: Keep your back flat and core engaged throughout.
Focus on pulling with your elbows.
Dumbbells allow each side of the back to work independently.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: A guided row variation that allows for heavy loading with a focus on mid-back contraction.
instructions: Position yourself in a bent-over stance over the Smith machine bar.
Grip the bar and unlatch it.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, keeping your back flat.
Lower the bar back down and repeat.
tips: Maintain a stable hinge position throughout the set.
The fixed path helps isolate the target muscles.
Adjust your distance from the bar for comfort.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Allows for a deeper range of motion and helps correct muscle imbalances in the back.
instructions: Place one knee and one hand on a bench for support, with your back flat.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with your arm extended toward the floor.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back and shoulder blade, not just your arm.
Maintain a stable torso and avoid rotating your body as you pull.
Keep your neck in a neutral position.
exercises.notesForLlm: Unilateral row that is easy to stabilize and progress.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.description: Essential for shoulder health, targeting the rear delts and upper back muscles.
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable pulley at upper-chest or eye level.
Grip the ends of the rope with your thumbs pointing back.
Pull the rope toward your forehead, pulling the ends apart as you get closer to your face.
Focus on squeezing your rear delts and mid-back at the end of the movement.
tips: Keep your elbows high and out to the sides.
Avoid using your lower back to pull; stay upright and stable.
Use lighter weights and focus on the quality of the contraction.
exercises.notesForLlm: Upper-back and rear-delt accessory often useful for shoulder balance.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: Isolates the rear part of the shoulders to help create a well-rounded physique.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench or stand and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back flat.
Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other and arms extended toward the floor.
Raise the weights out to the sides until your arms are level with your shoulders.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
tips: Focus on using your rear deltoids, not your traps.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Don't swing the weights.
exercises.notesForLlm: Rear-shoulder accessory with light loads and controlled tempo.

exercises.name: Machine Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: Isolates the rear deltoids using a machine for controlled and effective results.
instructions: Sit facing the machine with your chest firmly against the pad.
Grip the handles with your arms extended in front of you.
Pull the handles back in a wide arc until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your rear delts, then slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your chest against the pad to isolate the rear delts.
Focus on the contraction in the back of your shoulders.
Maintain a consistent, controlled tempo.
exercises.notesForLlm: Isolation for posterior deltoids; very easy to execute correctly compared to dumbbells.

exercises.name: Biceps Curl
exercises.description: The classic isolation exercise for building and defining the biceps.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing forward.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then slowly lower the weights back down.
Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid swinging your body or using momentum to lift the weights.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your torso.
Full range of motion: extend your arms fully at the bottom.
exercises.notesForLlm: Simple elbow-flexor accessory that pairs well with pulling days.

exercises.name: Cable Curl
exercises.description: A standing cable curl that keeps constant tension on the biceps from the start to the finish of every rep.
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ-style handle to a low cable pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the handle with palms facing up and keep your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the handle toward your shoulders while keeping your upper arms mostly still.
Lower the weight under control until your elbows are fully extended again.
tips: Do not let your shoulders roll forward as the weight lowers.
Keep your torso still and avoid leaning back to move the load.
Pause briefly near the top to maximize the biceps contraction.
exercises.notesForLlm: Cable biceps accessory with constant tension; straightforward substitute for dumbbell curls.

exercises.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
exercises.description: A behind-the-body cable curl that lengthens the biceps at the start of the rep and emphasizes the stretch position.
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley and stand facing away from the machine with the handle in one hand behind your hip.
Step forward until the cable pulls your working arm slightly behind your torso.
Curl the handle toward your shoulder while keeping your elbow from drifting too far forward.
Lower back to the stretched starting position with control before repeating.
tips: Set up enough distance from the machine to feel a stretch in the biceps at the bottom.
Keep your chest tall and avoid twisting your torso as you curl.
Use moderate loads and full control to get the most from the stretch.
exercises.notesForLlm: Behind-the-body unilateral cable curl, often called a Bayesian curl; excellent for biceps hypertrophy via the lengthened position.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.description: A neutral-grip curl that targets the biceps and the brachialis for thicker arms.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your torso (neutral grip).
Curl the weights up while maintaining the neutral grip.
Squeeze at the top and lower back down with control.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
tips: Focus on the contraction in your biceps and forearms.
Maintain an upright posture and avoid swaying.
Can be performed alternating arms or both together.
exercises.notesForLlm: Neutral-grip curl emphasizing brachialis and forearms.

exercises.name: Suspension Row
exercises.description: Uses a suspension trainer to perform bodyweight rows, allowing for easy difficulty adjustment via body angle.
instructions: Grip the handles and lean back with your arms extended and feet forward.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows back.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
tips: Adjust the difficulty by changing your foot position (closer to the anchor is harder).
Keep your core and glutes engaged to prevent your hips from sagging.
Focus on a smooth, controlled motion.
exercises.notesForLlm: Scalable bodyweight pull; angle determines intensity.

exercises.name: Landmine Row
exercises.description: A powerful back exercise performed by anchoring one end of a barbell and pulling the weighted end toward your torso.
instructions: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner on the floor.
Load weight plates onto the other end and straddle the bar, facing away from the anchor.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees slightly, keeping your back flat.
Grip the bar (using a V-handle if available) and pull the weighted end toward your lower ribs.
Lower the weight back down with control, maintaining a flat back.
tips: Brace your core throughout the movement to protect your lower back.
Focus on pulling with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Maintain a consistent hinge position; avoid 'bouncing' the weight up.
exercises.notesForLlm: Stable horizontal pull that allows for heavy loading with a unique mechanical advantage.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: A fundamental core exercise that builds isometric strength and stability across the entire midsection.
instructions: Place your forearms on the floor, elbows aligned under your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you and balance on your toes.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and hold the position.
tips: Avoid letting your hips sag or hike up too high.
Maintain a neutral neck position; look down at the floor.
Breathe steadily throughout the hold.
exercises.notesForLlm: Foundational anti-extension core drill that scales by duration and leverage.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: Focuses on the obliques and lateral core stability to improve balance and prevent back pain.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stack your feet.
Prop your upper body up on your forearm, with your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold the position while keeping your core engaged and hips level.
tips: Don't let your hips sag toward the floor.
Keep your neck in a neutral position, looking straight ahead.
For an easier variation, perform the plank with your knees on the floor.
exercises.notesForLlm: Lateral trunk stability drill useful for asymmetry management.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: A safe and effective way to build core stability and coordination without straining the back.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended toward the ceiling and knees bent at 90 degrees (tabletop position).
Slowly lower your right arm behind your head while simultaneously extending your left leg toward the floor.
Keep your lower back pressed firmly into the floor throughout the movement.
Return to the starting position and repeat with the opposite arm and leg.
tips: The key is to maintain a flat back; if your back arches, don't lower your leg as far.
Move slowly and with control.
Exhale as you extend your limbs.
exercises.notesForLlm: Low-risk trunk control drill appropriate in warmups and rehab-adjacent plans.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Improves balance and spinal stability by engaging the core, glutes, and shoulders simultaneously.
instructions: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Slowly extend your right arm forward and your left leg backward until both are parallel to the floor.
Keep your hips level and your core engaged to prevent your back from arching.
Hold for a second, then return to the starting position and switch sides.
tips: Imagine there is a glass of water on your back that you don't want to spill.
Don't lift your arm or leg too high; focus on length rather than height.
Keep your gaze toward the floor to maintain a neutral neck.
exercises.notesForLlm: Cross-body trunk stability drill that trains bracing and coordination.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
exercises.description: A dynamic exercise that targets the core while providing a significant cardiovascular challenge.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs, as if you are running in place in a plank position.
Keep your hips low and your core tight.
Maintain a consistent and rapid pace.
tips: Avoid letting your hips bounce up and down.
Focus on driving your knees straight forward.
Keep your weight centered over your hands.
exercises.notesForLlm: Conditioning drill that combines trunk stiffness with fast hip flexion.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.description: Targets the obliques with a rotational movement that improves core power and definition.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet slightly elevated.
Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Twist your torso to one side, bringing your hands toward the floor next to your hip.
Twist back to the other side in a controlled manner.
tips: Follow your hands with your eyes to ensure your entire torso is rotating.
Keep your feet together and as still as possible.
For added challenge, hold a weight or medicine ball.
exercises.notesForLlm: Rotational core drill best programmed with moderation and control.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: An excellent all-around core exercise that hits the upper abs, lower abs, and obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands behind your head and knees in a tabletop position.
Bring your right elbow toward your left knee while extending your right leg.
Switch sides, bringing your left elbow toward your right knee and extending your left leg.
Continue alternating sides in a pedaling motion.
tips: Focus on rotating your torso rather than just pulling your elbows.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Move with control rather than speed for better muscle engagement.
exercises.notesForLlm: Bodyweight trunk-flexion drill with some rotation and coordination demand.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: An advanced core exercise that specifically targets the lower abdominals and improves grip strength.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and a shoulder-width grip.
Keeping your legs straight (or slightly bent), lift them until they are parallel to the floor.
Lower your legs back down slowly and with control.
Avoid swinging your body to gain momentum.
tips: Engage your core and lats to stabilize your body.
Focus on the 'tucking' of your pelvis to engage your lower abs.
If full leg raises are too difficult, start with hanging knee raises.
exercises.notesForLlm: Advanced anterior-core exercise with high grip and shoulder demand.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.description: A functional rotational movement that builds core power and targets the obliques using cable resistance.
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with the handle set to high or low position.
Grip the handle with both hands and step away from the machine.
Pull the handle across your body and down (or up) in a diagonal woodchopping motion, rotating your torso.
Slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your arms mostly straight and rotate from your core.
Pivot your back foot as you rotate to protect your knees.
Maintain a stable base with your feet shoulder-width apart.
exercises.notesForLlm: Loaded rotational core pattern that should stay controlled rather than maximal.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.description: The ultimate full-body exercise for burning fat and building explosive power and endurance.
instructions: Start in a standing position.
Drop into a squat and place your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back into a plank position and perform a push-up.
Jump your feet back toward your hands and explosively jump into the air with your arms overhead.
tips: Maintain a tight core throughout the entire movement.
Land softly on your feet after the jump.
Can be modified by stepping back instead of jumping to reduce impact.
exercises.notesForLlm: Full-body conditioning drill with high fatigue cost; use sparingly.

exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
exercises.description: A classic total-body warm-up and conditioning exercise that improves coordination and cardiovascular health.
instructions: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump into the air while spreading your legs to shoulder-width and swinging your arms over your head.
Jump again to return to the starting position.
Repeat in a rhythmic fashion.
tips: Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
exercises.notesForLlm: Low-complexity conditioning drill excellent for warm-ups or active recovery in HIIT.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.description: A high-intensity cardio exercise that strengthens the legs and core while improving running form.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Lift your right knee toward your chest as high as possible while pumping your left arm.
Quickly switch legs, lifting your left knee and pumping your right arm.
Continue alternating at a fast pace, staying on the balls of your feet.
tips: Focus on lifting your knees to at least hip height.
Keep your torso upright; don't lean back.
Pump your arms to help maintain momentum.
exercises.notesForLlm: Dynamic conditioning drill that also builds hip flexor and core endurance.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.description: Combines a traditional squat with an explosive jump to build power and increase heart rate.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower into a squat position until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Explosively jump into the air, reaching as high as possible.
Land softly and immediately descend into the next squat.
tips: Absorb the impact by landing on the balls of your feet and rolling to your heels.
Ensure your knees don't cave inward during takeoff or landing.
Swing your arms to help generate upward power.
exercises.notesForLlm: Explosive lower-body power movement with high metabolic demand.

exercises.name: Butterfly Sit-Up
exercises.description: A classic Freeletics core exercise that uses a butterfly leg position to minimize hip flexor involvement.
instructions: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees pointing out.
Extend your arms overhead and touch the floor behind you.
Engage your core and sit up fully, touching the floor in front of your toes.
Lower yourself back down with control.
tips: Use your arms for momentum if needed, but focus on using your abs.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor during the initial phase of the sit-up.
Exhale as you sit up.
exercises.notesForLlm: Core flexion exercise favored in HIIT for its high rep potential and reduced hip flexor tension.

exercises.name: Sprawl
exercises.description: A 'down-and-up' movement similar to a burpee but without the push-up and jump, focused on speed and metabolic conditioning.
instructions: From a standing position, drop into a squat and place your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back into a high plank position.
Immediately jump your feet back toward your hands.
Return to a standing position as quickly as possible.
tips: Keep your core tight to avoid sagging your hips in the plank position.
Focus on quick transitions between standing and plank.
Maintain a steady rhythm.
exercises.notesForLlm: Faster, lower-impact alternative to burpees; great for conditioning.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight push-up variation performed in a pike position to target the shoulders and upper chest.
instructions: Start in a high plank position, then lift your hips until your body forms an inverted V-shape.
Keep your legs and arms straight, with your head tucked between your arms.
Lower the top of your head toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Push back up to the starting pike position.
tips: The closer your feet are to your hands, the more difficult the exercise becomes.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight.
Focus on pushing through your shoulders.
exercises.notesForLlm: Bodyweight vertical press alternative; bridge to handstand push-ups.

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.description: Strengthens the entire posterior chain, including the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor.
Hold the position for a second, squeezing your glutes and lower back.
Lower back down with control.
tips: Don't look up; keep your neck in a neutral position by looking at the floor.
Focus on length rather than height.
Breathe out as you lift.
exercises.notesForLlm: Isometric or rep-based posterior chain drill; excellent for posture and back health.

exercises.name: Hand-Release Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up variation where you lift your hands off the floor at the bottom of each rep to ensure a full range of motion and build explosive power.
instructions: Start in a high plank position.
Lower your chest all the way to the floor.
Briefly lift both hands off the floor, then place them back down.
Push explosively back up to the starting plank position.
tips: Maintain a tight core to avoid 'snaking' off the floor.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Focus on pushing through the entire palm.
exercises.notesForLlm: Standardized push-up variation that eliminates momentum and ensures full depth.

exercises.name: Climber
exercises.description: Similar to mountain climbers but with your feet jumping outside your hands, emphasizing hip mobility and core power.
instructions: Start in a high plank position.
Jump your right foot forward and place it outside your right hand.
Explosively switch legs, jumping your right foot back while bringing your left foot outside your left hand.
Continue alternating at a fast, rhythmic pace.
tips: Keep your hips as low as possible.
Focus on a large range of motion for your legs.
Maintain a strong, stable upper body.
exercises.notesForLlm: High-intensity conditioning drill that adds a mobility challenge to the standard mountain climber.

exercises.name: Boxing Bag Work
exercises.description: High-intensity intervals on the heavy bag build cardiovascular endurance, power, and coordination.
instructions: Stand in a boxing stance with your hands up guarding your face.
Perform various punches (jabs, crosses, hooks, uppercuts) against the heavy bag.
Stay light on your feet and move around the bag.
Maintain a high intensity for the duration of the round.
tips: Focus on proper punching technique to avoid wrist injury.
Exhale with every punch.
Keep your core engaged for more power and stability.
exercises.notesForLlm: Dynamic full-body conditioning with high metabolic demand.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.description: A gentle spinal movement that improves flexibility and relieves tension in the back.
instructions: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Cow: Inhale as you drop your belly toward the floor, lift your chest, and look up.
Cat: Exhale as you arch your back toward the ceiling, tuck your chin, and pull your belly button in.
Move smoothly between the two positions, following your breath.
tips: Focus on moving one vertebra at a time.
Keep your movements gentle and within a comfortable range of motion.
Spread your fingers wide for better support.
exercises.notesForLlm: Gentle spinal mobility drill suited to warmups and cooldowns.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: Relieves tightness in the hips caused by prolonged sitting or intense training.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front of you (half-kneeling position).
Keep your torso upright and gently push your hips forward.
Squeeze the glute of your kneeling leg to deepen the stretch.
Hold for the desired duration and then switch legs.
tips: Avoid arching your lower back; keep your core engaged.
You should feel the stretch in the front of your kneeling hip.
Maintain a tall posture throughout the stretch.
exercises.notesForLlm: Mobility drill useful after prolonged sitting and lower-body training.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: Improves flexibility in the back of the legs and helps prevent lower back pain.
instructions: Sit on the floor with one leg extended and the other foot against your inner thigh.
Hinge at your hips and reach toward your toes, keeping your back flat.
Hold the stretch when you feel tension in the back of your leg.
Repeat on the other side.
