tips: Don't bounce; hold a steady, gentle stretch.
Focus on reaching with your chest rather than your head to keep your back straighter.
Breathe deeply and try to relax into the stretch.
exercises.notesForLlm: Posterior-chain flexibility drill that should remain comfortable and controlled.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation
exercises.description: Opens up the upper back and improves rotational mobility for better posture and performance.
instructions: Start on all fours or in a side-lying position with knees bent.
Place one hand behind your head.
Rotate your elbow and torso toward the ceiling, following with your eyes.
Slowly return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your hips still and focus the rotation in your upper back.
Exhale as you rotate upward.
Don't force the range of motion; move within your comfort zone.
exercises.notesForLlm: Upper-back mobility drill that can help pressing and pulling comfort.

exercises.name: Shoulder Mobility Flow
exercises.description: A sequence of movements designed to improve range of motion and health in the shoulder joints.
instructions: Perform a series of controlled shoulder movements, such as arm circles, shoulder rolls, and 'wall slides'.
Move through each motion slowly and through its full range of motion.
Focus on keeping your shoulders relaxed and down away from your ears.
Maintain a steady, rhythmic flow.
tips: Avoid any movements that cause sharp pain.
Keep your core engaged to stabilize your torso during the arm movements.
Great as a warmup for any upper body workout.
exercises.notesForLlm: Shoulder-focused mobility sequence for warmups, cooldowns, and recovery days.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.description: A comprehensive dynamic stretch that targets the hips, hamstrings, and thoracic spine.
instructions: Start in a high plank position.
Step your right foot forward to the outside of your right hand.
Lift your right arm and rotate your torso toward the ceiling, looking at your hand.
Bring your right elbow down toward the inside of your right foot.
Push back into a hamstring stretch by straightening your front leg and lifting your toes.
Return to the plank and repeat on the other side.
tips: Move through each phase slowly and deliberately.
Keep your back leg as straight as possible during the rotation.
Focus on opening your chest as you rotate.
exercises.notesForLlm: Excellent full-body dynamic warmup movement that covers multiple planes of motion.

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose
exercises.description: An effective yoga pose for opening the hips and relieving tension in the glutes.
instructions: From a downward dog or all-fours position, bring your right knee forward toward your right wrist.
Place your right shin on the floor, aiming to have it parallel to the front of your mat (or as comfortable).
Extend your left leg straight back behind you.
Keep your hips square and slowly lower your torso over your front leg.
Hold and breathe into the stretch, then switch sides.
tips: Don't force your shin to be parallel if it causes knee pain.
Use a block or cushion under your hip for support if needed.
Keep your front foot flexed to protect your knee.
exercises.notesForLlm: Deep hip-opener targeting the piriformis and glutes; best used in cooldowns or for recovery.

exercises.name: Cobra Stretch
exercises.description: A gentle back extension that stretches the abdominal muscles and improves spinal flexibility.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended and tops of your feet down.
Place your hands under your shoulders.
Inhale and slowly straighten your arms to lift your chest off the floor.
Keep your hips on the floor and your shoulders away from your ears.
Look slightly upward and hold the stretch.
tips: Don't force your arms to be fully straight if it pinches your lower back.
Engage your glutes slightly to support your spine.
Focus on length through the front of your body.
exercises.notesForLlm: Gentle spinal extension useful for counteracting prolonged sitting and stretching the anterior chain.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.description: A restful pose that gently stretches the back, hips, and shoulders.
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your big toes touching and sit on your heels.
Separate your knees about hip-width apart.
Exhale and lean forward, resting your torso between your thighs.
Extend your arms forward with palms down, or rest them by your sides.
Rest your forehead on the floor and breathe deeply.
tips: Widen your knees further to make more room for your torso if needed.
Focus on sending your breath into your lower back.
Relax your jaw and shoulders completely.
exercises.notesForLlm: Relaxing recovery pose; excellent for decompressing the spine at the end of a session.

exercises.name: Inchworm
exercises.description: A dynamic movement that stretches the hamstrings while building core and shoulder stability.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at your hips and place your hands on the floor (bend knees slightly if needed).
Walk your hands forward until you reach a high plank position.
Pause briefly, then walk your feet toward your hands using small steps while keeping legs as straight as possible.
Return to a standing position and repeat.
tips: Maintain a tight core to avoid sagging your hips during the plank.
Keep your legs straight as long as possible to maximize the hamstring stretch.
Move with control, avoiding rushing.
exercises.notesForLlm: Great dynamic warmup that combines posterior chain mobility with core activation.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.description: A simple shoulder mobility exercise that warms up the rotator cuff and improves joint health.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Perform small, controlled circles with your arms in a forward direction.
After the desired duration, reverse the direction to backward circles.
Gradually increase the size of the circles as your shoulders feel warmer.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and down away from your ears.
Maintain a stable torso; don't let your body rock.
Breathe naturally throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Leg Swings
exercises.description: A dynamic stretch that improves hip mobility and prepares the legs for training.
instructions: Stand near a wall or sturdy object for balance.
Swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled motion, increasing the range as you go.
After the desired reps, switch to side-to-side swings across your body.
Switch legs and repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright and core engaged; avoid excessive arching of the back.
Don't force the range of motion; stay within a comfortable stretch.
Maintain a rhythmic, steady tempo.
exercises.notesForLlm: Effective dynamic hip warmup often used before lower-body or running sessions.

exercises.name: Wrist Circles
exercises.description: Improves wrist joint mobility and helps prevent strain during upper-body exercises.
instructions: Extend your arms in front of you or keep them relaxed at your sides.
Rotate your wrists in a circular motion, moving through the full range of motion.
Perform circles in both clockwise and counter-clockwise directions.
You can also interlace your fingers and rotate your wrists together.
tips: Keep the movement slow and focused.
Relax your hands and fingers.
Particularly useful before exercises like push-ups or bench press.
exercises.notesForLlm: Specific joint mobility for the wrists, useful for those with desk jobs or prior wrist issues.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
exercises.description: Enhances ankle mobility and prepares the feet for weight-bearing activities.
instructions: Stand on one leg (using a wall for balance) or sit with one leg extended.
Rotate your ankle in a circular motion, drawing the largest circle possible with your toes.
Perform circles in both directions.
Switch feet and repeat.
tips: Focus on moving only the ankle, not the whole leg.
Move slowly to ensure you hit every part of the rotation.
Great for improving squat depth and running mechanics.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
exercises.description: An isometric hold in the bottom of a squat to improve hip, knee, and ankle mobility.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Lower into your deepest possible squat, keeping your heels on the floor.
Rest your elbows on the inside of your knees to gently push them outward.
Keep your chest as upright as possible.
Hold the position for the desired duration, breathing deeply.
tips: If your heels lift, place them on a small elevation or hold onto a sturdy object for balance.
Focus on relaxing into the hips.
Gently shift your weight from side to side to target different areas.
exercises.notesForLlm: Excellent for improving squat mechanics and lower-body mobility; can be used in warmups or as a standalone daily practice.

exercises.name: Scapular Circles
exercises.description: Improves shoulder blade (scapula) mobility and health, promoting better posture and upper-body mechanics.
instructions: Stand or sit upright with arms relaxed at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears (elevation).
Pull them back, squeezing your shoulder blades together (retraction).
Drop them down as far as possible (depression).
Push them forward, rounding your upper back slightly (protraction).
Smooth these movements into a circular motion, performing both directions.
tips: Keep your arms straight and still; the movement should come from the shoulder blades.
Imagine drawing a circle with the points of your shoulders.
Avoid arching your lower back.
exercises.notesForLlm: Key drill for shoulder health and posture; highly recommended before any pressing or pulling.

exercises.name: Quad Stretch
exercises.description: A classic stretch for the front of the thigh to improve flexibility and knee health.
instructions: Stand on one leg, using a wall or chair for balance if needed.
Bend your other knee and reach back to grab your foot or ankle with the same-side hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glutes.
Keep your knees together and your torso upright.
Hold and then switch legs.
tips: Squeeze your glutes of the stretching leg to deepen the stretch in the hip flexor.
Avoid arching your lower back.
Ensure you're standing tall, not leaning forward.

exercises.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.description: Uses a doorway or frame to open up the chest and front of the shoulders, counteracting 'hunched' posture.
instructions: Stand in a doorway or at the corner of a wall.
Place your forearm(s) against the doorframe with the elbow at shoulder height.
Gently lean or step forward until you feel a comfortable stretch in your chest.
Hold the position, breathing deeply.
You can adjust the height of your arms to target different parts of the chest.
tips: Don't lean too far; the stretch should be gentle.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Keep your core engaged to avoid arching your lower back.
exercises.notesForLlm: Excellent postural stretch for those with tight pecs or forward-rounded shoulders.

exercises.name: Scorpions
exercises.description: A dynamic stretch for the hips, lower back, and chest performed while lying face down.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended out to the sides in a 'T' shape.
Lift your right leg and reach it across your body toward your left hand, rotating your hips.
Try to touch the floor with your right foot while keeping your chest and arms as flat as possible.
Return to center and repeat with the left leg.
tips: Move slowly and with control to protect your lower back.
Focus on the rotation of the spine and opening of the hips.
Only reach as far as is comfortable; your foot doesn't have to touch your hand.
exercises.notesForLlm: Dynamic rotational mobility drill useful in warmups for athletes and those with healthy backs.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
exercises.description: A gentle rotation for the upper back and shoulders that also stretches the neck.
instructions: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Reach your right arm under your body to the left, sliding the back of your hand along the floor.
Lower your right shoulder and ear toward the floor.
Keep your hips square and breathe into the stretch between your shoulder blades.
Hold, then return to center and repeat on the other side.
tips: Focus on the stretch in the upper back and rear shoulder.
Use your left hand to gently press into the floor and deepen the rotation if comfortable.
Relax your neck completely.
exercises.notesForLlm: Calming thoracic mobility and shoulder stretch; great for recovery and evening routines.

exercises.name: Neck Circles
exercises.description: Gently releases tension in the neck and improves cervical range of motion.
instructions: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed.
Gently drop your chin toward your chest.
Slowly roll your head toward one shoulder, then carefully toward the back, and over to the other shoulder.
Continue the circular motion slowly and smoothly.
Reverse directions after the desired duration.
tips: Avoid any rapid or jerky movements.
If you feel any sharp pain or dizziness, stop immediately.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed throughout.
exercises.notesForLlm: Simple neck mobility; should be done with caution and slow speed.
